summary:
[  edit  ]
The Filter  CHOP  smooths or sharpens the input channels. It filters by combining each sample and a range of its neighbor samples to set the new value of that sample. Each filter type uses its own weighting factors for the neighboring samples. The  Filter Width  determines the number of neighbors to use.
The default Gaussian filter nicely smooths out data, typically with a Filter Width around .3 seconds. The Box Filter is interesting when your inputs are step changes to new values: the values linearly interpolate to the new value.
It is useful to follow the Filter  CHOP  with a  Trail CHOP  and connect the filtered and pre-filtered signal to its inputs.
If you want to pass one or more channels in, each with multi-samples, and you want to filter each sample as if each sample was its own filter, turn on the  Filter per Sample  parameter.
For a similar, more-abrupt effect, see the  Lag CHOP .
The Filter  CHOP  can filter both motion and sound, but other CHOPs are more appropriate for filtering sound (see the  Audio Filter CHOP ,  Band EQ CHOP , and  Parametric EQ CHOP ).

Notes on the One Euro  Filter    [  edit  ]
The one Euro Filter is especially useful when a person is in an interaction loop with TouchDeigner and wants quick response: It responds quickly to large changes in value, and it smooths out jitters in the input:
Cutoff Frequency: Decrease it if slow speed jitter is a problem.
Slope Cutoff Frequency: Avoids high derivative bursts caused by jitter. (The research paper implementation fixes this value to 1Hz but defaults to )
Speed Coefficient: Increase if high speed lag is a problem.
The 1 € filter ("one Euro filter") is a simple algorithm to filter noisy signals for high precision and responsiveness. It uses a first order low-pass filter with an adaptive cutoff frequency: at low speeds, a low cutoff stabilizes the signal by reducing jitter, but as speed increases, the cutoff is increased to reduce lag. The algorithm is easy to implement, uses very few resources, and with two easily understood parameters, it is easy to tune. In a comparison with other filters, the 1 € filter has less lag using a reference amount of jitter reduction. (researchgate.net)
Here is a procedure to tune the One Euro filter:
First Speed Coefficient is set to 0 and Cutoff Frequency to a reasonable middle-ground value such as 1 Hz. Then the body part is held steady or moved at a very low speed while Slope Cutoff Frequency is adjusted to remove jitter and preserve an acceptable lag during these slow movements (decreasing Slope Cutoff Frequency reduces jitter but increases lag, Slope Cutoff Frequency must be > 0). Next, the body part is moved quickly in different directions while Speed Coefficient is increased with a focus on minimizing lag. First find the right order of magnitude to tune Speed Coefficient, which depends on the kind of data you manipulate and their units: do not hesitate to start with values like 0.001 or 0.0001. You can first multiply and divide Speed Coefficient by factor 10 until you notice an effect on latency when moving quickly. Note that parameters Speed Coefficient and Speed Coefficient have clear conceptual relationships: if high speed lag is a problem, increase Speed Coefficient. If slow speed jitter is a problem, decrease Slope Cutoff Frequency.
reference: Casiez, G., Roussel, N. and Vogel, D. (2012). 1€  Filter : A Simple Speed-based Low-pass Filter for Noisy Input in Interactive Systems

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: type
parameters.description: ⊞  - There are seven types of filters:

parameters.label: Gaussian
parameters.name: gauss
parameters.description: This filter has a Gaussian (normal or "bell" curve) shape that smooths the channel. It acts as a low pass filter. The wider the filter, the lower the cutoff frequency, resulting in smoother data.

parameters.label: Left Half Gaussian
parameters.name: halfgauss
parameters.description: This produces a lag on the channel. If the input channels represent values over time, this filter is seen as only using samples back in time from the current sample. For time-data, this is more realistic as you can't look ahead in time. (Maybe some day.) It has a half-bell shape.

parameters.label: Box
parameters.name: box
parameters.description: This filter is box-shaped, meaning that each neighbor sample it uses has the same weighting factor. It can produce unwanted steps in the output channel because the effect of the samples at the extremes of the filter don't fade out as the window slides over the samples. It low-pass filters data, similar to the Gaussian filter.

parameters.label: NOTE: When using Gaussian or Box filtering, the channel is delayed by half the filter size (i.e. a Filter Size of 30 samples will delay the output by 15 samples). To eliminate this delay, use either a Left Half Gaussian or a Left Half Box filter. Applying a Sharpen or Edge Detect filter always delays the output by half the filter size. Applying a Despike filter will delay the output by the full filter size.     Left Half Box
parameters.name: halfbox
parameters.description: This filter produces a lag on the data, uses only samples back in time, and otherwise acts like a box filter.

parameters.label: Edge Detect
parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: This filter detects "edges", sharp changes in the input channels. It acts as a high pass filter. As the filter width is increased, more low frequencies are added.

parameters.label: Sharpen
parameters.name: sharpen
parameters.description: This filter sharpens all high frequencies. It is the sum of the edge detect result and the original data.

parameters.label: De-spike
parameters.name: despike
parameters.description: This filter removes "spikes" (samples more than `Spike Tolerance' above or below the expected sample value). The filter width allows you to eliminate spikes that are several samples long. Wide filters will remove wide spikes (spikes of several samples) and small filters will only remove narrow spikes (one or two samples in length).

parameters.label: Ramp Preserve
parameters.name: ramp
parameters.description: This filter attempts to output an increasing ramp that increases at the 'Ramp Rate' parameter rate. The input channel to the Filter  CHOP  should be increasing at this rate, with possibly some errors/noise in it. The Ramp Preserve will ignore the input channel unless the difference between the input value and the current ramp value is larger than 'Ramp Tolerance' parameter. When the difference becomes greater than the tolerance, the ramp will reset to start at the current input value.

parameters.label: One Euro
parameters.name: oneeuro
parameters.description: This filter is good for filtering noisy signals while maintaining high precision and resposiveness.

parameters.label: Effect
parameters.name: effect
parameters.description: The extent to which the filter affects the channel (0 - not at all, 1 - maximum effect).

parameters.label: Filter Width
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The amount of surrounding samples used in the calculation of the current sample. It is expressed in the Units.

parameters.label: Filter Width Unit
parameters.name: widthunit
parameters.description: Choose between using Samples, Frames, or Seconds as the units for this parameter.

parameters.label: Spike Tolerance
parameters.name: spike
parameters.description: For the De-spike filter type, this is the amount that a sample can differ from its neighbours without being considered a spike.

parameters.label: Ramp Tolerance
parameters.name: ramptolerance
parameters.description: When using a Ramp Preserve filter, if the input value deviates from the current output ramp value by this much, then the ramp will reset to the new input value. Otherwise the Ramp Preserve will continue climbing at the specified 'Ramp Rate'.

parameters.label: Ramp Rate
parameters.name: ramprate
parameters.description: When using a Ramp Preserve filter, this is the rate that the  CHOP 's output channel will increase. Only if the input channel value deviates from the desired output value by 'Ramp Tolerance' amount will the  CHOP  instead output the input channel value.

parameters.label: Number of Passes
parameters.name: passes
parameters.description: The number of times the filter is applied to the channel.

parameters.label: Cutoff Frequency (Hz)
parameters.name: cutoff
parameters.description: Decrease it if slow speed jitter is a problem.

parameters.label: Speed Coefficient
parameters.name: speedcoeff
parameters.description: Increase if high speed lag is a problem.

parameters.label: Slope Cutoff Frequency (Hz)
parameters.name: slopecutoff
parameters.description: Avoids high derivative bursts caused by jitter.

parameters.label: Slope Down Reset
parameters.name: slopedownreset
parameters.description: When On resets (bypasses) the filter effect when the downward slope exceeds the Slope Down Max value to the right.

parameters.label: Slope Down Max
parameters.name: slopedownmax
parameters.description: Set the maximum value of the slope downwards beyond which the filter resets when the toggle to the left is On.

parameters.label: Slope Up Reset
parameters.name: slopeupreset
parameters.description: When On resets (bypasses) the filter effect when the upward slope exceeds the Slope Up Max value to the right.

parameters.label: Slope Up Max
parameters.name: slopeupmax
parameters.description: Set the maximum value of the slope upwards beyond which the filter resets when the toggle to the left is On.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: When On resets (bypasses) the filter effect.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Instantly resets the filter effect.

parameters.label: Filter per Sample
parameters.name: filterpersample
parameters.description: Applies the filter to each sample of the channel instead of across the whole channel. Useful for working with multi-sample channels.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: Rename from
parameters.name: commonrenamefrom
parameters.description: The channel pattern to rename. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Rename to
parameters.name: commonrenameto
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the names. The default parameters do not rename the channels. See  Pattern Replacement .

parameters.label: Channel Names:  c[1
parameters.description: 10:2] ambient

parameters.label: Rename To:  b[1
parameters.description: 5] amb    This example fetches channels  c1 c3 c5 c7 c9  and  ambient .

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
